title: Bollinger %B
summary: Shows where price sits inside its own Bollinger Bands, with 0 at the lower band, 1 at the upper band and readings beyond them outside the bands.
descriptionHtml:
Bollinger %B turns the position of price inside its bands into a single number. The bands are a simple average of the source plus and minus a multiple of its standard deviation. %B is the source minus the lower band, divided by the width between the bands, so 0 is the lower band, 0.5 the middle and 1 the upper band.

The study keeps a running sum and sum of squares over the last Period values and divides by the number of values seen so far, so the bands and %B exist from the first bar rather than after a warmup. The standard deviation is the population form. A window with no spread gives bands of zero width, and %B then reads 0.5.
howToReadHtml:
A reading above 1 means price closed above the upper band, and a reading below 0 means it closed below the lower band. Readings above 0.8 and below 0.2 mark the upper and lower parts of the band, and 0.5 is the moving average. In a strong uptrend %B can stay above 0.8 for many bars, so a high reading is a description of strength, not automatically a sell signal.

Comparing %B highs with price highs is a common use: a new price high with a lower %B high says price is less stretched relative to its volatility than it was before.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: Number of bars in the average and the standard deviation. Longer periods give smoother bands that react more slowly.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series placed within the bands, the close by default.

settings.label: StdDev Multiplier
settings.html: How many standard deviations the bands sit from the average. A larger value widens the bands and keeps %B nearer 0.5.

faq.html: Yes. Above 1 means price is above the upper band, below 0 means it is below the lower band. The scale is not capped.

faq.q: Why does the line start on the first bar?
faq.html: Until the window fills, the average and the deviation use the bars seen so far, so there is a value from the start. The first few bars rest on very little data.

faq.q: What does a reading of exactly 0.5 on a flat market mean?
faq.html: When every value in the window is the same, the bands have no width. The study reports the midpoint, 0.5, in that case.

related.summary: Plots the gap between a fast and a slow exponential average in price units, with a correction that removes the starting bias on early bars.
